3246.title: Merge lane is too slow for 40 merges a day: one extra tick per merge, and the next PR waits for the next tick
3246.body:
## Problem
The merge lane is too slow for the goal of 40 merges per day. It takes one PR at a time, and it moves only on the 10-minute tick. Each merge also loses one extra tick:
- `enterLane` adds the label `pdd:merge-lane` and then reads the label list at once.
- GitHub's list does not show the new label yet, so the tick returns "wait" (`if (!now.length) return 'wait'`).
- The next tick, 10 minutes later, finds the label and goes on.
When the lane frees, the next green PR waits for the next tick too.

## Evidence
- Chaos test note 4 (Nov 11, 0.1.28): every merge cost one more tick because of the label read lag.
- Sandbox merges came 30 to 50 minutes apart (median 30 minutes). So the lane does at best about one merge per 30 minutes, about 48 per day with no gaps at all.
- The target is 40 merges per day (Nov 13).

## Proposal
- After the lane label write, read the PR's own labels (`GET issues/N`) in the same tick, which is consistent. Do not wait for the list to catch up.
- When the lane frees (a merge, an END or a release of the lane holder), run the next lane step for the next green PR at once, in the same tick.

## Test
- A fake GitHub whose label list is empty right after the write, while the PR's own labels show the lane. Expect the lane step to go on in the same tick.
- Two green PRs in the queue. After the first merges, expect the second to enter the lane in the same tick.
- Core factory timing: two queued green PRs merge in fewer ticks than today.

3249.title: Keep a checklist from the issue, apart from the builder's scope, and show which items the evidence covers
3249.body:
## Problem
The builder decides the scope of its PR. Nothing keeps the full list of what the issue asks for. So a PR can pass every check and still leave items of the issue undone, and it is called complete.

## Evidence (funnel audit, Nov 9 17:00 to Nov 11 17:00 UTC)
- pdd #2892: the first PR (#3165, old engine) left checklist items of the issue pending. A later core PR (#3222) covered the full docs issue.
- pdd #3012: the work lacked the pilot that the issue requires.
- Narrow passing tests did not show the whole outcome.

## Proposal
- At job start, the engine takes a checklist from the issue text: task-list items, "Done when" and "Expected" sections, and acceptance criteria. It keeps this list apart from the builder's scope.
- The PR body lists each item with its evidence (a test, a check or a file), or with an exclusion that the issue supports (a quote).
- The fresh reviewer checks each item. An item with no evidence and no supported exclusion is a must-fix.
- The merge note shows "checklist: N of M covered".

## Test
- A fake issue with 3 checklist items, and a PR that covers 2. Expect a review must-fix that names the third item, and no merge.
- The same PR with a quoted exclusion from the issue for the third item. Expect a pass.
- An issue with no checklist. Expect no checklist line and no new red.

3260.title: Autopilot waits forever when GitHub Actions does not start a run (personal account minutes or spending limit)
3260.body:
## Problem
Autopilot waits forever when GitHub Actions does not start a run. This is common for a person's private repository: GitHub gives a fixed number of free Actions minutes per month, and the spending limit is often $0. Many people will run Autopilot on a repository like that, not in an organization with paid minutes.

## Evidence (Nov 11)
- From about 20:20 UTC, no Actions run started in the private repositories of one personal account (our sandbox and a new-user trial repository). The runs stayed "queued" with no job, and GitHub refused to cancel them. GitHub's status page said Actions worked. Repositories in the organization ran normally.
- The sandbox PR #106 had a review PASS and a green local full suite at its exact head (198/198 at 20:39 UTC). It waited in the merge lane for more than an hour with no CI result. Nothing merged, and nothing told the person why.
- This week the sandbox used many Actions minutes: each repair push starts a new CI run.

## Proposal
1. Detect it. A CI run for the PR head that stays queued with no started job for 20 minutes, or that fails with a GitHub billing or spending-limit message, means "CI did not start".
2. Do not blame the issue. This is a service-owned stop: no strike, no END, no repair.
3. Tell the person once. One line in `pdd autopilot status` and one alert: "GitHub Actions does not start runs in this repository (queued since HH:MM). This is often the account's Actions minutes or spending limit: Settings → Billing → Actions." No repeated alerts.
4. Hold new intake while CI does not start, so agents do not use tokens on work that cannot merge. Resume by itself when a CI run starts again.
5. Merge rule when CI does not start (decision below):
   - A: wait until CI works.
   - B: when the repository has no required status check, merge on the local full suite that Autopilot already runs on the exact head, and write "CI: did not start (reason); local full suite passed at HEAD" in the merge note. When a required check exists, wait (A).
6. Use fewer minutes:
   - the CI workflow that pdd setup writes uses `concurrency` with `cancel-in-progress`, so a new push cancels the old run;
   - Autopilot opens PRs as drafts and marks them ready only at the final head, with the workflow running on ready PRs only.
7. `pdd autopilot doctor` shows the Actions minutes left when the GitHub token can read billing, and says how to grant that.

## Test
- A fake GitHub whose CI run stays queued: after 20 minutes the job is held with the service reason, one alert, no strike, and new intake stops. When a run starts, intake resumes.
- Rule B with no required check: the PR merges with the CI line in the note. With a required check: it waits.
- The setup workflow has the concurrency group, and a second push cancels the first run.

## Decision
A or B as the default.

Related: #3246 (merge lane), #3181 (red main), #3238 (stop owners), #3242 (new users).
